sections.title: Extreme co-design and the AI factory

items.q: Why doesn't NVIDIA win by building "the best chip" alone anymore?
items.a: **Extreme co-design**: GPU, CPU, memory, networking, storage, power, cooling, software, racks, pods, and data centers are one system. Distributed AI hits **Amdahl's Law** — networking/CPU/memory/power all become bottlenecks. The unit of compute is now a **gigawatt-scale token factory**.

items.q: How does Jensen organize the company around that stack?
items.a: Org charts should **mirror the product**, not generic hamburger charts. He has **60+ direct reports** (almost all engineers) who attack problems in **group sessions** — no one-on-ones — because every design choice ripples across the stack.

items.q: What is NVIDIA's primary competitive moat?
items.a: "**Install base** defines an architecture. Not… Everything else is secondary." **CUDA on every GeForce** built developer reach before cloud existed — "NVIDIA is the house that **GeForce** built" — plus horizontal ecosystem integration across industries and clouds.

items.q: What are the four AI scaling laws Jensen describes?
items.a: **Pre-training, post-training, test-time/inference, and agentic** — they loop as agents generate data back into training. "Inference is thinking… Thinking is way harder than reading." Token cost drops ~**10×/year**; NVIDIA scaled compute ~**1M× in 10 years** vs Moore's Law ~**100×**.

items.q: How should AI data centers use the power grid smarter?
items.a: The grid runs ~**60% of peak ~99% of the time**. Use that **idle capacity** and gracefully degrade during rare peaks instead of demanding **six-nines** uptime for every watt.

items.q: How complex is a modern NVIDIA rack supply chain?
items.a: About **200 suppliers** and **1.3M components** per Vera Rubin rack. Jensen informs upstream/downstream CEOs like employees — notably **no formal contract with TSMC** after decades of trust.
Compare every design against **physical limits**, not incremental 74→72-day improvements. "We need things to be as complex as necessary, but as **simple as possible**."

items.q: Will AI eliminate jobs like radiology?
items.a: Separate **job purpose from tasks**. The radiologist scare was wrong — purpose and headcount grew. Hire people **expert in using AI**; coding expands from ~**30M** to ~**1B** as specification artistry. "You can outsource your thinking, but you can't outsource your **understanding**."

Under a **billion-dollar-company** definition — agents can already spin up viral apps — he says "I think we've achieved **AGI**." Building NVIDIA-scale companies remains human. **Intelligence is a commodity**; humanity (pain, love, subjective experience) is bigger — chips won't feel nervous.

items.q: How does Jensen prepare people before big bets?
items.a: **Belief-system shaping**: reason about the future daily and align employees, partners, and board **before** announcements so everyone says "what took you so long?" Resilience stack includes childlike "**How hard can it be?**," forgetting setbacks, and sharing burden quickly.
